Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

word noun

also in a word, word for word, not a word, first words

classical

Hor. S. 1.1.120–121: verbum nōn amplius addam
Quint. 1.2.6: nōndum prīma verba exprimit

verbum, verbī n.

noun, second declension

Ūnō verbō, in a word (Cic. Fin. 2.73); ad verbum, word for word (Cic. Fin. 1.4); meīs verbīs, from me, in my name (Cic. Att. 16.11.8). For verba dare see word, promise.

Examples

  • jam satis est. … verbum nōn amplius addam

    That’s enough now. … I won’t add another word.Hor. S. 1.1.120–121

  • nōndum prīma verba exprimit, jam coccum intellegit, jam conchȳlium poscit.

    He can’t say his first words yet, but he already knows scarlet and asks for purple.Quint. 1.2.6

  • hās prīmum audiet puer, hārum verba effingere imitandō cōnābitur

    these the child will hear first, and theirs are the words he will try to copyQuint. 1.1.5

  • Bona verba, quaesō.

    Don’t say such things, please!Ter. And. 204

Other words

  • vocābulum, vocābulī n. — a word as the name of a thing

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Gell. 4.1.18: rem nōn suō vocābulō dēmōnstrāre; M-O s.v. term

    Lewis & Short: “an appellation, designation, name of any thing”.

  • vōx, vōcis f. — a word as spoken, a saying; voice

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Fin. 2.6 (Lewis & Short): quid sonet haec vōx voluptātis

See also I want a word with you, name, language, alphabet, word, mean.
